faq.answer: No. Charisma may be trained, role-required, culturally expected, or rewarded by an audience. The wing hypothesis needs recurring Type Two connection attention plus visibility-shaped delivery that persists across matched settings.
faq.question: Does charismatic helping establish 2w3?

faq.answer: Observe what remains central when credit disappears. A 2w3 hypothesis keeps another person's need and relational response in view; a Three hypothesis may organize attention more around achievement, effectiveness, and image.
faq.question: How does 2w3 differ from a Three hypothesis?

faq.answer: Private help that remains equally steady, little adaptation to audience response, or action fully explained by targets and incentives would weaken the modifier hypothesis. Off-role examples are especially useful.
faq.question: What observation weakens visible effectiveness?

sections.body_md: A 2w3 interpretation begins with Type Two attention to needs, then asks whether Three-adjacent adaptation and visible impact shape delivery. Charisma or efficiency without recurring connection attention may reflect work skill, leadership, incentives, or audience training.
sections.title: Start with connection, then test visibility

sections.body_md: A sibling comparison contrasts 2w3 adaptive, visible effectiveness with 2w1 principled and restrained service. Compared with Three, the proposed core remains another person's need and relational response rather than achievement or image alone.
sections.title: Contrast 2w3 with 2w1 and Three

sections.body_md: Compare a public event, a private favor, and a task where someone else receives credit. Record whether the offer adapts to actual need, whether contribution continues without visibility, and whether recognition changes warmth or follow-through.
sections.title: Observe private and public contribution

sections.body_md: A 2w3 counterexample weakens a visible effectiveness hypothesis when help remains equally engaged without an audience, presentation does not shift with response, or achievement goals explain the action while connection attention is absent.
sections.title: Use private consistency as a challenge

sections.body_md: Sales, fundraising, community leadership, hospitality, and customer success reward adaptive warmth and visible results. Compare off-role behavior, private contribution, incentives, and status before attributing the style to a wing.
sections.title: Test performance and customer roles

sections.body_md: Wing evidence is limited, so 2w3 remains a secondary observation hypothesis rather than an independent category. It establishes no charisma, leadership value, moral worth, fixed ability, or future result.
sections.title: Do not turn effectiveness into identity proof

sections.body_md:
Duration: 5

Context: Choose one public contribution, one private favor, and one shared task where another person receives the visible credit.

Observable signal: Record the need noticed, audience response, adaptation made, recognition available, and whether follow-through changes when visibility drops.

Page-specific signal: Compare useful action that tracks real need with presentation that tracks applause, status, targets, or access to a visible role.

Alternative explanation: Test sales training, leadership duty, hospitality norms, performance targets, fundraising skill, and reputation incentives against 2w3.

Reflection prompt: Identify the event best explained by achievement or audience reward rather than connection and state how the wing hypothesis changes.

seo.description: The 2w3 wing is a core-first, evidence-limited hypothesis: Type Two attention to needs and connection may be modified by Three-adjacent adaptability, presentation, and visible effectiveness. Effective help can also reflect sales, leadership, hospitality, or performance incentives rather than a wing.
seo.title: 2w3: visible effectiveness as a core-first wing hypothesis
